title: Temptation
definition: Temptation refers to the biblical truth about humanity’s condition before God.
summary: Temptation refers to the biblical truth about humanity’s condition before God.
christFocus: Jesus reveals both true humanity and the saving grace fallen humanity needs.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Temptation teaches that Scripture tells the truth about human dignity, responsibility, corruption, and need for grace. Scripture tells the truth about humanity without denying dignity and without minimizing the ruin sin has brought.

God gives this truth so people may stop hiding and come into the light. People need clarity about themselves before they can understand the mercy of christ. The Bible’s honesty is mercy because what remains hidden cannot be healed rightly.

Christ enters the truth this doctrine exposes. Jesus reveals both true humanity and the saving grace fallen humanity needs. In Him, sinners are not left under guilt, shame, bondage, fear, or death; they are called to repentance, faith, restoration, and new life by the power of the Holy Spirit.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People need this truth because sin, shame, weakness, and brokenness are not solved by denial. People need clarity about themselves before they can understand the mercy of christ. Scripture tells the truth so that people may stop hiding and come to Christ.

It also protects believers from shallow answers. Humanity needs forgiveness, new birth, restoration, and Spirit-empowered obedience, not merely better circumstances or stronger willpower.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Respond with humility, repentance, and trust in Christ. Bring this doctrine into prayer, Scripture, and daily obedience. Ask the Holy Spirit to make the truth real in your thinking, desires, relationships, and next faithful step with Christ.
